Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

### Modifications in Each File

1. **`xe_device_types.h`**:
   - Added a new member to the `struct xe_device`:
     - `struct workqueue_struct *preempt_fence_wq;` - This is used to serialize preempt fences.

2. **`xe_device.c`**:
   - In the `xe_device_destroy` function:
     - Added a check to destroy the `preempt_fence_wq` if it is initialized.
   - In the `xe_device_create` function:
     - Allocated the `preempt_fence_wq` using `alloc_ordered_workqueue("xe-preempt-fence-wq", 0);`.
     - Updated the error handling to include a check for the successful allocation of `preempt_fence_wq`.

3. **`xe_preempt_fence.c`**:
   - Modified the `preempt_fence_enable_signaling` function:
     - Changed the work queue from `system_unbound_wq` to `q->vm->xe->preempt_fence_wq` for queuing the preempt work.

### Relationships Between Modifications

The modifications across the three files are interconnected to address the issue of starvation in the `system_unbound_wq` when multiple preempt fences are waiting. 

- The addition of `preempt_fence_wq` in `xe_device_types.h` establishes a dedicated work queue for handling preempt fences, which is crucial for avoiding contention with other system processes.
- The changes in `xe_device.c` ensure that this new work queue is properly created and destroyed, maintaining resource management and preventing memory leaks.
- Finally, the update in `xe_preempt_fence.c` shifts the queuing of preempt work from the general `system_unbound_wq` to the newly created `preempt_fence_wq`, ensuring that preempt fence operations are serialized without affecting other system operations. 

Overall, these modifications collectively enhance the handling of preempt fences in the DRM driver for Intel GPUs, improving system stability and performance.

Here is the commit message:
drm/xe: Use ordered wq for preempt fence waiting

Preempt fences can sleep waiting for an exec queue suspend operation to
complete. If the system_unbound_wq is used for waiting and the number of
waiters exceeds max_active this will result in other users of the
system_unbound_wq getting starved. Use a device private work queue for
preempt fences to avoid starvation of the system_unbound_wq.

Even though suspend operations can complete out-of-order, all suspend
operations within a VM need to complete before the preempt rebind worker
can start. With that, use a device private ordered wq for preempt fence
waiting.

v2:
 - Add comment about cleanup on failure (Matt R)
 - Update commit message (Lucas)

Fixes: dd08ebf6c352 ("drm/xe: Introduce a new DRM driver for Intel GPUs")
Signed-off-by: Matthew Brost <matthew.brost@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Lucas De Marchi <lucas.demarchi@intel.com>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20240401221913.139672-2-matthew.brost@intel.com
Signed-off-by: Lucas De Marchi <lucas.demarchi@intel.com>
(cherry picked from commit 37c15c4aae1fe3f67efd2641db8d8c25c2d524ab)
Signed-off-by: Lucas De Marchi <lucas.demarchi@intel.com>

Here is the root cause:
The root cause of the bug is that preempt fences can sleep while waiting for an execution queue suspend operation to complete. If the `system_unbound_wq` is used for this waiting and the number of waiters exceeds the maximum active limit, it can lead to starvation of other users of the `system_unbound_wq`, causing performance issues and potential deadlocks in the system. This situation arises because suspend operations can complete out-of-order, and all suspend operations within a virtual machine (VM) need to finish before the preempt rebind worker can start.

Here is the patch:
 
 static bool preempt_fence_enable_signaling(struct dma_fence *fence)
 {
 	struct xe_preempt_fence *pfence =
 		container_of(fence, typeof(*pfence), base);
 	struct xe_exec_queue *q = pfence->q;
 
 	pfence->error = q->ops->suspend(q);
-	queue_work(system_unbound_wq, &pfence->preempt_work);
+	queue_work(q->vm->xe->preempt_fence_wq, &pfence->preempt_work);
 	return true;
 }

```c

```
Reason:
Using `system_unbound_wq` for waiting on preempt fences can lead to starvation of other users of this work queue if the number of waiters exceeds the maximum active limit. This is problematic because suspend operations can complete out-of-order, and all suspend operations within a VM must finish before the preempt rebind worker can start, potentially causing performance issues and deadlocks.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
queue_work(q->vm->xe->preempt_fence_wq, &pfence->preempt_work);
```
Reason:
By using a device private ordered work queue (`preempt_fence_wq`) instead of the `system_unbound_wq`, the patch ensures that preempt fences wait without affecting the performance of other users of the system-wide work queue. This change allows for proper synchronization of suspend operations within a VM, preventing starvation and ensuring that all necessary operations complete in the correct order.
